title: Rewind to the first input position
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $start$ be a state of $M$, and let $w$ be a Boolean input word. Suppose $c$ is a configuration on input $w$ with one more work tape than $M$, with control state $0$ among three numbered states. For either Boolean value $ok$, if $c$ is in control state $0$, then starting from the same configuration with its state renamed to the rewind phase carrying $ok$, the split-body machine reaches, after some $t \le r+2$ steps, a configuration with the same tapes, work-head positions, and output as $c$, input-head position $1$, and control state $2$, where $r$ is the initial input-head position of $c$. At every time $j \le t$ in this run, the machine is not in its anchor state.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$c$ is a configuration on input $w$ with $M.k+1$ work tapes and three numbered control states
The state of $c$ is control state $0$
